Namespace Tuinet.Widgets

Classes

EditableText

The editing core of Tuinet.Widgets.TextInputState and Tuinet.Widgets.TextAreaState: the text, a caret with an optional selection, movement by grapheme cluster and by word, and undo/redo. Offsets count UTF-16 chars and fall on grapheme cluster boundaries. The text lives in a gap buffer, so typing in the middle costs about what typing at the end does. Allocates only when the text or the undo history outgrows its buffers, and when Tuinet.Widgets.EditableText.Text is read after an edit.

Spinner

Animation frames for activity indicators. Pick a frame from elapsed time, not frame count.

Table

Helpers for Tuinet.Widgets.Table`1.

TextAreaState

Editable multi-line text for Tuinet.Widgets.TextArea: a gap buffer with a line index, caret and selection, undo/redo, soft wrap, and the viewport the last render showed (for keys and the mouse). Owned by the app. Lines end with '\n'; pasted CR LF and CR become '\n' and tabs four spaces. Rendering only measures the lines on screen, so a frame costs the same for 10 lines or 100,000.

TextInputState

Editable single-line text: emacs-style editing keys, Shift+movement selection, undo/redo and optional masking, on the shared Tuinet.Widgets.EditableText core. The caret moves and deletes by grapheme cluster (an emoji sequence or a letter with its accents is one step). Line breaks and other control characters are dropped. Owned by the app.

TreeState

Expanded nodes, selection and scroll position of a tree, owned by the app. The visible rows are cached as flat arrays (node, parent row, depth, guide bits), rebuilt only when the tree's shape changes: expanding, collapsing or Tuinet.Widgets.TreeState.Invalidate. Tuinet.Widgets.TreeState.Handle``1(Tuinet.KeyEvent,``0), Tuinet.Widgets.TreeState.HandleMouse``1(Tuinet.MouseEvent,``0,System.Int32), Tuinet.Widgets.TreeState.Select``1(System.Int32,``0) and render take the source and rebuild first, so a frame costs O(visible rows) however deep the view is scrolled. The selection follows its node across rebuilds; if an ancestor collapsed, the ancestor is selected.

Structs

Bar

One bar of a Tuinet.Widgets.BarChart. Style is layered over Tuinet.Widgets.BarChart.BarStyle.

BarChart

Bars that compare values, with eighth-block ends. Tuinet.Direction.Vertical bars grow up from the bottom, Tuinet.Widgets.BarChart.BarWidth wide, with the label under each bar and the value above it (inside its top when the bar is full height). Tuinet.Direction.Horizontal bars grow right, one row each, after a label column as wide as the widest label (at most a third of the width), with the value after the bar. Bars that don't fit are dropped from the end. Zero, negative and NaN values draw no bar; values over Tuinet.Widgets.BarChart.Max are clamped.

Block

A frame with optional title and footer on its top and bottom edges.

Button

A one-row button: the label padded by two cells each side, filled with its style.

Checkbox

A checkbox: symbol, space, label on one row; or, with Tuinet.Widgets.Checkbox.Boxed, a 5×3 rounded box (about square, since cells are twice as tall as wide) filled when checked, label to its right.

Clear

Blanks an area with a style. Render it first to draw a popup over existing content.

Dropdown<TSource>

A select box: Tuinet.Widgets.Dropdown`1.Render(Tuinet.Rect,Tuinet.CellBuffer,Tuinet.Widgets.DropdownState@) draws the closed field (selected item + '▾'); after drawing everything else, call Tuinet.Widgets.Dropdown`1.RenderPopup(Tuinet.Rect,Tuinet.CellBuffer,Tuinet.Widgets.DropdownState@) so the open list sits on top.

DropdownState

Committed choice, open flag and highlighted row of a Tuinet.Widgets.Dropdown`1.

ListState

Selection and scroll position of a list. Owned by the app, updated by input and by render. Render scrolls to keep Tuinet.Widgets.ListState.Selected visible whenever it changes (or the list is resized); in between, Tuinet.Widgets.ListState.Offset can scroll on its own, e.g. with the mouse wheel.

ListView<TSource>

A scrolling, selectable list over any Tuinet.Widgets.IListSource.

Menu

A popup list of actions: labels with mnemonics, right-aligned shortcuts, separators joined to the border and disabled items. Size it with Tuinet.Widgets.Menu.Measure(System.ReadOnlySpan{Tuinet.Widgets.MenuItem}) and place it with Tuinet.Rect.PlaceNear(Tuinet.Rect,Tuinet.Size), by the row it belongs to or at a 0×0 point at the pointer; render it last so it sits on top. The area is the box: a Tuinet.Widgets.Popup.Shadow hangs off it. A menu taller than its area scrolls to keep the highlight in view.

MenuItem

One row of a Tuinet.Widgets.Menu. An '&' in Tuinet.Widgets.MenuItem.Label marks the next letter as its mnemonic (drawn with Tuinet.Widgets.Menu.MnemonicStyle; pressing it activates the item); "&&" is a literal '&'. Items are values: build the array once and swap one in with with { Enabled = … } to change it.

MenuState

The highlighted item and scroll position of a Tuinet.Widgets.Menu, and where it was drawn. Owned by the app.

Paragraph

Multi-line text ('\n'-separated) with wrapping, alignment and vertical scroll, in one style or styled runs.

Popup

A box drawn over existing content: an optional drop shadow, a fill and a Tuinet.Widgets.Block, in one call. The area includes the shadow (the last two columns and the last row), so the box itself is Tuinet.Widgets.Popup.Frame(Tuinet.Rect). Stateless: keep the rect you rendered into for hit-testing, e.g. click outside to close.

ProgressBar

A horizontal bar filled to Tuinet.Widgets.ProgressBar.Ratio on the first row of its area. With the default '█' fill, the boundary cell uses eighth-blocks (▏▎▍▌▋▊▉) for sub-cell precision.

Scrollbar

A scroll position indicator: a thumb sized Tuinet.Widgets.Scrollbar.Viewport / Tuinet.Widgets.Scrollbar.Content of the track, placed at Tuinet.Widgets.Scrollbar.Position. Drawn along the first column (vertical) or row (horizontal) of its area. With the default '█' thumb, its ends use eighth-blocks for sub-cell precision.

Sparkline

A value over time in eighth-block columns (▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█), one value per column, newest on the right. With several rows the levels stack, so h rows give 8h levels. Given more values than columns, it shows the last ones. Zero draws nothing; NaN and negative values leave a gap; any other positive value shows at least ▁.

Table<TSource>

A scrolling, selectable table: a header row over virtualized rows, laid out in columns with per-column alignment. Selection and scroll live in a Tuinet.Widgets.ListState, as for Tuinet.Widgets.ListView`1.

TableColumn

One column of a Tuinet.Widgets.Table`1: header text, width and how cells sit in it.

Tabs

A one-row tab bar: titles with padding, separated by Tuinet.Widgets.Tabs.Divider. When they don't fit, it scrolls to keep the selected tab visible and shows ‹ › where tabs are hidden. Only the tabs are drawn; the rest of the row is left as it is, so the bar can sit in a Tuinet.Widgets.Block's top border.

TabsState

Selected tab and scroll position of a Tuinet.Widgets.Tabs bar. Owned by the app. Render scrolls to keep Tuinet.Widgets.TabsState.Selected visible whenever it changes (or the bar is resized); in between, Tuinet.Widgets.TabsState.Offset can scroll on its own, e.g. with the overflow arrows or the wheel.

TextArea

Draws a Tuinet.Widgets.TextAreaState: the lines in view, soft-wrapped or scrolled sideways, with optional line numbers, a placeholder, and when Tuinet.Widgets.TextArea.Focused the selection and the real terminal cursor at the caret. Only visible lines are measured.

TextInput

Draws a Tuinet.Widgets.TextInputState on the first row of its area, scrolled to keep the caret visible. When Tuinet.Widgets.TextInput.Focused, places the real terminal cursor at the caret and shows the selection.

TextItems

A list source over strings, drawn in one style and clipped with an ellipsis.

TextRows

A table source over rows of strings (row-major), drawn in one style. Missing cells are blank.

TreeView<TSource>

A scrolling, selectable tree over any Tuinet.Widgets.ITreeSource. Each row is its guides (├─, └─, │), an expander for nodes with children ([+] collapsed, [-] expanded), then the label. Only visible rows are drawn. Selection, the highlight symbol and the scrollbar work as in Tuinet.Widgets.ListView`1.

Interfaces

IListSource

Items for a Tuinet.Widgets.ListView`1. Only visible rows are rendered (virtualized).

ITableSource

Rows for a Tuinet.Widgets.Table`1. Only visible rows are asked for (virtualized).

ITreeSource

A hierarchy for a Tuinet.Widgets.TreeView`1: app-owned data addressed by integer node ids the app chooses (an index into its own array, or a key into a dictionary). The tree must not have cycles.
